title: The 247 CMR 9.04 requirements that do not apply to institutional sterile compounding pharmacies
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.04(15), the requirements of 247 CMR 9.04(4), (5), (6), (9), (10), (12), (13) and (14) do not apply to institutional sterile compounding pharmacies. The excluded requirements include the counting rule in 9.04(10), under which a pharmacist deciding whether a prescription is within date counts the day after the prescription was written as day one; the Schedule VI rule in 9.04(12), under which a Schedule VI prescription is valid for one year from the date of issue and may not be refilled after one year; the Schedule V rule in 9.04(13), under which a Schedule V prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue or refilled more than five times; and the refill record in 9.04(6), under which a pharmacist refilling a Schedule III-VI prescription records the date of dispensing, the amount dispensed and his or her initials.
exam_relevance: Tests that the facility carve-out in 247 CMR 9.04(15) reaches the day-count, Schedule VI and Schedule V rules alike, so a figure from any of them is checked against the facility type before it is applied.
common_confusions: Applying the Schedule V six-month and five-refill limits of 247 CMR 9.04(13) at an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy.
Assuming the carve-out reaches only 247 CMR 9.04(13), when it also lists the counting rule in 9.04(10) and the Schedule VI rule in 9.04(12).
verification_notes: 247 CMR 9.04(6), (10), (12), (13) and (15) read on 2026-09-11 in the official Board of Registration in Pharmacy text published on mass.gov (pages stamped 12/6/24). Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
